card.name: Words just before intubation or procedure terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words or partial words in anesthesia and hospital-procedure text, such as 'for' after succinylcholine or 'attempting' before intubation. It marks the spot where a procedure or care-setting term is about to come.

modes.label: Before intubation
modes.description: A linking word or verb right before the word intubation or airway securing.
modes.example: following the use of succinylcholine<< for>> intubation under balanced anesthesia.

modes.label: Start of a drug or procedure name
modes.description: The first letter or two of a word like cuffed or Cisatracurium, partway into a term.
modes.example: the airway should be secured with a<< c>>uffed endotracheal tube before attempting

modes.label: Linking word before a clinical action
modes.description: A word such as 'for', 'local' or 'e.g.,' that leads into a procedure or practice.
modes.example: non–cross-matched ABO/RhD-compatible RBCs can be given as per<< local>> blood bank practices

card.writes: It seems to push toward Chinese hospital-department words like 科 and 护 (nursing), and toward 'ward'.
card.plain: It fires on little words that come just before a hospital procedure such as intubation.
